newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean supermarket sales higher in July.
newsitem.headline: Chilean supermarket sales higher in July.

text.p: Chilean supermarket sales rose 9.2 percent in July in real terms over the same month in 1995, and rose 16.3 percent in nominal terms, the National Statistics Institute said.
But sales slipped 3.7 percent in real terms last month with respect to June and fell 3.5 percent measured nominally, said the institute.
Supermarket sales are watched as a barometer of the health of consumer spending.
In the first seven months of the year, supermarket sales rose 12.2 percent in real terms over the same period last year, and 20.7 percent in nominal terms, said the institute.

Calculations in real terms are based on a constant index of supermarket prices used as a deflator, said the institute. A total of 549 stores, 160 of them in Santiago, with three or more cash registers are used in drawing up the indices, it said.
